extracted.intended_audience: individuals or organizations seeking to submit petitions for rulemaking to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for members of the public (individuals, advocacy groups, businesses) on how to prepare and submit petitions for rulemaking to the CFPB, what to include, how submissions will be handled, and the subsequent docketing/comment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Your contact information (full name, address, telephone number, email address).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full name, mailing address, telephone number, and email so the CFPB can notify the petitioner if the submission is docketed. Petitions will not be edited to remove any identifying or contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of action requested
rubrics_metrics.description: The type of action you are requesting (e.g., whether the CFPB should issue a new rule or repeal or amend an existing rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state whether you request issuance of a new rule, amendment of an existing rule, or repeal so CFPB can characterize and process the petition appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation that submission is a petition under APA §553(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: State that it is a petition under section 553(e) of the Administrative Procedure Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CFPB recommends explicitly stating this to assist in review and consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual and legal reasons for the proposed action
rubrics_metrics.description: The factual and legal reasons for the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide supporting factual evidence and legal arguments explaining why the requested rulemaking, amendment, or repeal is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected effects of the proposed action
rubrics_metrics.description: The expected effects the proposed action will have on relevant parties (e.g., consumers, industry, enforcement authorities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe anticipated impacts on stakeholders to help the CFPB assess benefits, burdens, and reach of the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods and addressing
rubrics_metrics.description: You can submit your petitions for rulemaking by emailing petitions@cfpb.gov or by mail, hand delivery, or courier to the Rulemaking Petitions Docket at the CFPB address provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure proper handling, the CFPB recommends submitting petitions only through these methods. Provide the specified address/attn line when using mail, hand delivery, or courier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure / do not include sensitive information
rubrics_metrics.description: All petitions, including attachments and other supporting materials, will become part of the public record and subject to public disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include proprietary information or sensitive personal information such as account numbers, Social Security numbers, or names of other individuals. Submissions will not be edited to remove identifying/contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials CFPB may decline to post
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFPB may, in its discretion, decide not to post submissions and other materials, or portions thereof, including duplicate identical submissions, copyrighted material owned by someone other than the submitter, confidential business information (CBI), spam submissions, threats of harm or violence, and submissions that are disavowed by the named author or submitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid submitting material that falls into these categories if you expect public posting; proprietary/CBI should be handled accordingly and copyrighted third-party content should only be submitted with permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing and public comment process
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission is determined to be a petition, it will be assigned a docket number and posted to Regulations.gov for public comment. The petitioner will be notified once the petition has been docketed. After the comment period closes, the CFPB will review the petition and any submitted comments and issue a final response. The final response will also be posted to the docket on Regulations.gov and to this webpage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a public comment period once docketed; CFPB review and a final response follow. Use the docket on Regulations.gov to follow status and view related comments and final responses.
